current_indicator_source: World Development Indicators, World Bank (source id 2)
current_indicator_source_note: The price level index (PLI) is the ratio of a purchasing power parity (PPP) conversion factor to the corresponding market exchange rate between two countries, expressed relative to a base country that is set equal to 100. For this series the base country is the United States. It provides a measure of the differences in price level between the country and the United States by indicating the number of units of the common currency (US dollars) needed to buy the same volume of the aggregation level in each country. At the level of GDP, the price level ratio provides a measure of the differences in the general price levels of countries.
transformation: ratio = current_indicator raw value / 100. The current indicator is expressed on a 0-100 scale with base country United States = 100; the retired indicator was expressed as a direct ratio (United States = 1.0) of the same underlying measure (PPP conversion factor to market exchange rate, base United States) per both indicators' own sourceNote text. Dividing by 100 restores the ratio scale the band thresholds below assume.
